What the streams say

    Metric

    The ride film

    Route, terrain and sensors on one shared cursor. Move the pointer over any panel — or use ← → once a panel has focus — to scrub. Drag across a profile to zoom into that stretch.

    Terrain — colour is gradient

    Descent reads cool, climbing reads warm, flat road is neutral grey. Bins are steeper than −10%, then −10 to −6, −6 to −3, −3 to −1.2, flat, +1.2 to +3, +3 to +6, +6 to +10, and steeper than +10%.

    Power

    Climb ledger

    Every sustained ascent the elevation stream contains, found by drawdown segmentation: a rise closes once the road gives back 25 m. Kept if it climbs ≥ 100 m over ≥ 1 km at ≥ 3%. Select a row to zoom every profile to that climb.

    Detected climbs with their terrain and sensor averages
    Climb At km Length Gain Avg % Max % Cat Time VAM Power HR Cad Torque Temp

    The fade

    The same four measures across the ten climbs, in ride order. Each panel carries its own scale — this is four separate one-series charts sharing an x-axis, not one chart with four y-axes.

    Climb-by-climb values

    Aerobic efficiency drift

    Rolling 20-minute normalised power divided by rolling heart rate — watts bought per heartbeat. A falling line is cardiac drift: the same effort costing more beats. Windows with more than 15% stopped time are dropped.

    Efficiency by 20 km block

    Pedalling signature

    Where the seconds actually went in the cadence × torque plane — the two things whose product is power. Same colour scale across both panels, so the panels are directly comparable. Coasting, sub-30 rpm and sub-30 W samples excluded.

    Cadence distribution, climbing vs flat

    Left/right balance

    Median left-leg share per five-minute block, from the pedal-based balance stream. 50% is symmetric; the band marks ±2%. Only samples above 60 W count.

    Balance by 20 km block

    Time in zone

    Two separate distributions, each on its own scale. Ordered bands use one hue, dark to light.

    Zone totals

    —

    Built from one workout's raw sensor streams. Elevation is smoothed over a 120 m distance window before gradient and climb detection; gradient is a ±40 m central difference clamped to ±25%. The GPS track starts 76 samples after the other sensors — satellite acquisition — and is re-aligned to them here.
